guards.what: G1 (LIVE): CardModel.CreateClone() is a full model clone; the sim rebuilds the card from its id, so the copy loses the original's enchantment, affliction, keyword edits and cost modifiers
guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-29 (round 7): `create_clone` (cards/base.py) IS a memberwise copy now. `ClonePreservingMutability` is `AbstractModel.MutableClone` (a MemberwiseClone) and only THEN `DeepCloneFields` (CardModel.cs:1193-1216) and `AfterCloned` (:1218-1239), so the sim opens with `clone.__dict__.update(card.__dict__)` and the two override passes only re-point what must not be shared (`combat`, and the enchantment/affliction that DeepCloneFields re-creates). Everything the guard named now rides along: the LIVE KEYWORD SET (`_keywords = GetKeywordsWithSources(KeywordSources.Local)`, :1196-1200 -- Music Box's Ethereal), the cloned `_energyCost` and its `_localModifiers` (:1202 -> CardEnergyCost.cs:411-421 -- SetThisCombat, AddThisTurn, free-this-turn), the cloned `_dynamicVars` (:1201 -- a grown Rampage clones grown) and `BaseReplayCount` (Hidden Gem). `CreateClone`'s own tail, `ExhaustOnNextPlay = false` (:2178), is the last line. ONE MORE FINDING, and it is the reason the fix could not be a one-liner: DeepCloneFields re-attaches with `EnchantInternal` (:1204-1209 -> :1491-1498), which checks NO CanEnchant and does NOT run `ModifyCard` -- EnchantmentModel.cs:350-353 says why in as many words, "It is NOT called when a card is cloned, because the enchantment's effects will already be reflected in the card's values." The sim only had the normal `attach`, and re-running it on a memberwise copy is not merely redundant, it THROWS for Souls, whose CanEnchant demands the Exhaust its own ModifyCard removes. `Enchantment.attach_internal` is that path. EXECUTED, old -> new: keyword False->True, free-this-turn cost 1->0, base_replay_count 0->3, a twice-played Rampage 9->19. Pinned by test/test_create_clone_memberwise.py. TEST MOVED (non-negotiable 5): test_card_clone_enchantment.py's `test_clone_reapplies_a_static_card_modification` is now `test_clone_carries_a_static_card_modification`, with the reason inline; its assertion is unchanged. NOT CLOSED: nothing at this site.  The text it replaced read: NARROWED 2026-07-27, RE-OPENED 2026-07-28: the copy carries MORE per-instance state than it used to, but it is still REBUILT, not cloned. CLOSED: sts2_rl/relics/music_box.py:47 calls `create_clone(card)` (sts2_rl/cards/base.py:57-83) instead of `make_card(card.id)` plus a hand-rolled upgrade replay, and create_clone carries the source's upgrade level, a live copy of its ENCHANTMENT (clone_preserving_mutability) and a live copy of its AFFLICTION -- two of the four components this guard names. STILL OPEN: create_clone's first statement is `clone = type(card)()` (cards/base.py:74), a rebuild from the class, where CardModel.CreateClone -> CardScope.CloneCard -> MutableClone is a MEMBERWISE copy whose DeepCloneFields (CardModel.cs:1193-1216) additionally re-clones `_keywords` (GetKeywordsWithSources(KeywordSources.Local)), `_dynamicVars`, `_energyCost` (`_energyCost?.Clone(this)`) and `_temporaryStarCosts`, and whose AfterCloned (CardModel.cs:1218-1239) resets only CurrentTarget / CurrentPlayIndex / DeckVersion / HasBeenRemovedFromState and the event handlers. So exactly the other two components this guard names -- KEYWORD EDITS and COST MODIFIERS -- are still dropped, along with `base_replay_count` (CardModel.BaseReplayCount). EXECUTED 2026-07-28: `c = make_card('strike'); c.set_cost_this_combat(0); c.base_replay_count = 1; c.is_ethereal = True` gives source (energy_cost 0, replay 1, ethereal True) and `create_clone(c)` gives (1, 0, False). The state exists and is written on live paths -- cards/base.py backs _cost_delta_this_turn / _free_this_turn / _cost_this_turn / _cost_this_combat / base_replay_count, and potions.py, powers.py, enchantments.py, cards/stomp.py and relics/mummified_hand.py all write them -- so a Music Box copy of an Attack whose cost was cut this turn/combat arrives at full cost in the sim and at the modified cost in the game. Rule 7: sts2_rl/potions.py, sts2_rl/enchantments.py, sts2_rl/cards/stomp.py and sts2_rl/relics/mummified_hand.py are not hashed by this record.

guards.rationale: Checked deliberately because the same mechanism is a LIVE gap at three other relics in this batch (mummified_hand G3, nunchaku G1, ornamental_fan G1). Here the relic's own guards absorb it: C# fires BeforeCardPlayed and AfterCardPlayed once per play-count iteration (CardModel.cs:1929, :1959, inside the loop opened at :1904), and iteration 0's AfterCardPlayed sets `WasUsedThisTurn = true` and `CardBeingPlayed = null` (MusicBox.cs:81-82), so iteration 1's BeforeCardPlayed bails at MusicBox.cs:61 and no second copy is made. CardCmd.ApplyKeyword is `card.AddKeyword(keyword)` plus a visual refresh (CardCmd.cs:676-683); the sim models Ethereal as the `is_ethereal` flag on Card (cards/base.py:62), which is what the end-of-turn ethereal pass reads. Rule 7: CardCmd.cs and cards/base.py are unhashed here.

AddGeneratedCardsToCombat (CardPileCmd.cs:202-249) bails when the combat is not in progress, records a CardGenerated history entry, routes through Add(card, pile) and then fires Hook.AfterCardGeneratedForCombat. cmds.py appends to the hand (overflowing to the discard pile at MAX_HAND_SIZE) and calls CardPileCmd._enter_combat; its own docstring names AddGeneratedCardToCombat as the mirror. The history entry is the game's save bookkeeping, which the sim's conformance layer reads rather than writes. Rule 7: CardPileCmd.cs and cmds.py are unhashed here, and the hand-overflow equivalence rests on cmds.py's docstring rather than on a line of CardPileCmd.cs that I read.
